Base directory for this skill: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/skills/jusprin-release

# Making a JusPrin release

`.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml` builds one commit into a draft
release. It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes, a guide
check and the Sentry secrets (see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not
run tests, check the server, check translations or audit error handling.
This skill covers all of it, in order.

## Kenneth decides these

Ask, and wait for his yes before each one. A yes covers that action only.

- The version, when he has not named it, and the release notes' wording.
- Deploying the server.
- Which error-handling findings must be fixed before the release.
- Taking in commits that landed on `jusprin-dev` after the range was fixed.
- Spending API money (say the cost).
- Every push, and moving `main`.
- Starting the release workflow.
- Downloading the draft's files.
- The Sentry values and read-only token for checking the draft.
- Posting anything on GitHub.

Never publish the draft: Kenneth does, by hand. Never force-push `main`.

## When something has to be fixed

A fix is its own commit on `jusprin-dev`, made in a worktree of its own from
`origin/jusprin-dev`, never in the release commit. Once it is pushed:

- **Before section 8 landed the release commit:** rebase your branch onto
  `origin/jusprin-dev`, record that as the new end of the range, and redo
  step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7.
- **After it landed:** keep the version. Redo step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7
  up to the fix, land what changed (section 8), move `main` and start the
  workflow again. A new run for the same version replaces the draft.

## Where each platform is tested

Every release is tested on all three platforms, twice: the test suites
(section 5) and the draft's own files (section 10). An untested platform
blocks the release.

- **macOS:** this computer.
- **Windows and Linux:** the two Google Cloud test VMs. How to reach, start,
  build on and run the app on each is in
  `<main checkout>/.claude/vm-harness/windows/README.md` and `…/linux/README.md`.
  That folder is local to this computer, never in the repository. Start a
  stopped VM, and stop it again when done. If a VM or that folder is
  missing, stop and tell Kenneth.

## 1. Set up

1. The main checkout (the folder holding `jusprin-dev`) must have no changed
   tracked files and no commits missing from `origin/jusprin-dev`. If it has
   any, list them for Kenneth and wait; never push, commit or discard them
   yourself. Untracked files are his working docs and do not block.
2. The range is the newest `jusprin/v*` tag to the current
   `origin/jusprin-dev`. Record that commit: every later step checks this
   range, and section 8 checks whether `jusprin-dev` moved.
3. Settle the version, then make a worktree at that commit under
   `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`, on branch `claude/release-<version>` (add a
   suffix if taken). Never name a branch `jusprin-release/...`: pushing one
   starts an unsigned release build.
4. Read every commit in the range for what a person would notice and the
   GitHub issues it fixes.

## 2. Version and release notes

1. `kVersion` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`.
2. `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`, shaped like
   the previous one, for a person who prints. It becomes the draft's text on
   every workflow run, and an older app shows it under "Release notes" in
   Preferences › Updates. Check every on-screen label you quote against the
   source.
3. Anything new the app sends from the person's computer goes in the notes,
   with what it holds.

## 3. Server readiness

Every address the release calls must already answer on
`https://jusprinv2.obico.io`. Many are joined from pieces, so list them from
the code that builds them and write out each full path:

```bash
git grep -n -E '"/(ent|o|accounts|jusprin)/|"/models"|ask_server\("' -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin ':!*test*'
```

For example `ask_server("code/confirm", …)` is
`/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/code/confirm`, and the model list is the gateway's
address with its last part replaced by `/models`. A bare GET with no sign-in
or real data is enough: any 4xx answer except 404 means the address is there.

First GET a made-up address such as `/ent/jusprin/v2/no-such-address`: it
must answer 404. In maintenance mode the server answers 200 for every path,
and the check cannot tell anything apart; stop and tell Kenneth.

A missing address means the server change is not deployed. Find it in
tsd-enterprise (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py` on `master`) and tell Kenneth,
along with any other server behavior the range relies on. Deploying is his
call.

## 4. Error-handling audit

Run the `error-handling` skill on the range. When the release relies on
server changes, also audit tsd-enterprise's `web_ent/jusprin/` commits on
`master` since the previous tag's date (that repository has no release tags).
Report the findings and wait for Kenneth to say which must be fixed.

## 5. Tests

Build in your worktree in Release, following "Building on a shared machine"
in `AGENTS.md`. Use CMake.app's cmake (Homebrew's fails to find Eigen3), node
on `PATH`, and absolute paths.

The app builds against the main checkout's dependency folder, which may
predate a dependency the range added or changed. Bring it up to date first:

```bash
<worktree>/scripts/deps_current.sh <main checkout>/deps/build/arm64
```

It compares the `deps/` recipe the folder was last built from with the
worktree's, and when they differ it rebuilds the libraries that changed. If
it says the main checkout's recipe differs from the worktree's, the main
checkout is not at the end of the range; stop and tell Kenneth.

```bash
cmake -S <worktree> -B <worktree>/build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<main checkout>/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
cmake --build <worktree>/build/arm64 --config Release --target tests/all jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs -- -j4
ctest --test-dir <worktree>/build/arm64/tests -C Release --output-on-failure -LE RequiresApp
```

`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` takes one path only. `tests/all` builds every test
program, including `shell_integration_harness` for the guide check.
`agent_live_tests` is built but never registered with ctest, since each run
is billed. Also run `npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI`.

- **Windows and Linux,** on the VMs, from a checkout of the end of the range:
  `build_win.bat -s --run-tests`, and `./build_linux.sh -st` then
  `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release --output-on-failure`, keeping the
  `RequiresApp` tests, which run only on Linux.
- **Prompt suites,** when the range changes text the model reads: run
  `tests/project_prompt` (and `tests/printer_prompt` when printer chats
  changed) on the free `claude-cli` backend. Its README also asks for a small
  paid run on the app's default model before a release; propose it with its
  cost.

To tell whether the range caused a failure, run the same test on a build of
the last release's tag. A failure there too is older: report it and let
Kenneth decide. One the range caused is a bug to fix before the release.

## 6. Translations

After the audit and tests, since a fix can add a sentence.

1. Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py` (needs GNU
   gettext and `npm ci` in `AgentUI`). Changed catalogs go in the release
   commit.
2. Translate new entries in JusPrin's own catalogs, `Localization/native/`
   and `Localization/pages/`, as `Localization/README.md` says. Never touch
   upstream's `localization/i18n/` or run `run_gettext`; from `AGENTS.md` and
   the `orca-translations` skill take only the editing rules and glossary.
3. `npx vitest run src/catalogs.test.ts` in `AgentUI` must pass.
4. Rebuild `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs` for the guide check.
5. Tell Kenneth how many entries are marked `# Needs human review`.

No tool finds a sentence nobody marked for translation; look for one while
reading the range.

## 7. Guide check

Follow "Before a release" in `docs/guide/README.md`, on the step 5 build.

1. Tell Kenneth first: it drives the app on this Mac's screen, and nobody
   should use the computer meanwhile.
2. Add new screens or menu items from the range to the guide before the
   check: it cannot find them, and a page changed after it passes is
   unchecked.
3. Run `<worktree>/scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. The script checks the
   tree it sits in, so the main checkout's copy checks the wrong code. It
   writes `docs/guide/checked-version.txt` when it passes.

## 8. Commit and land

1. The release commit holds `Version.hpp`, the notes, the catalogs, and what
   the guide check changed: `docs/guide/` (pages, `pictures/`,
   `checked-version.txt`) and `AgentUI/src/skills/guide-*/`. Nothing else.
2. If `origin/jusprin-dev` moved past the recorded end of the range, list the
   new commits for Kenneth. With his yes, rebase and redo step 1.4 and
   sections 2 to 7. If he says no, the release waits: your branch cannot
   reach `jusprin-dev` without them.
3. With his yes, push to `jusprin-dev` without a merge commit, then
   `git -C <main checkout> pull --ff-only`. If that pull is refused, stop and
   tell Kenneth without changing the main checkout.
4. With his yes, move `main` to that exact release commit, as a fast
   forward only.

## 9. Start the release workflow

The publisher is the repository variable `JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER`, or
`kennethjiang` when unset; `gh api user -q .login` must print it. This
computer's `gh` token cannot read repository variables or secrets (403), so
the workflow's first job is what reports a wrong publisher or a missing
Sentry secret (`JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`,
`SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`). Only Kenneth can add a secret.

With his yes:

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true
```

Keep Mac signing on: Homebrew refuses an unsigned Mac app. Check that the new
`workflow_dispatch` run is on the release commit. If its "Upload to the draft
release" job waits for an approval (the `release` environment can require
one), tell Kenneth. A failed run is reported with its log, never worked
around with a skip box.

The Mac jobs build on GitHub's Macs. If GitHub has no Mac machine for the
repo, they end "cancelled" 15 minutes after they were queued, with no runner
and no steps. GitHub can also cancel a Mac job that is already building, for
lack of capacity: its log then ends with only "The operation was canceled".
Either way, tell Kenneth. With his yes, start the run again on Kenneth's own
Mac (the self-hosted runner, user `jusprin-ci`):

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true -f self_hosted_mac=true
```

## 10. Test the draft

Test the draft's own files: the Mac disk image on this computer, the Windows
installer and the AppImage on their VMs. Install over the previous release,
check that Preferences shows the new version, have one chat and slice, and
check each fix in the notes on the platform where it mattered. Kenneth signs
in, or you use a test account he names; never type a password. A chat spends
that account's credits.

Never print the app's settings file (the `.conf` file in its data folder), on
the VMs or here: it holds saved API keys and sign-ins, and whatever a command
prints stays in the session's log. Read or change the one setting you need,
such as the language, with a command that prints only that setting.

Sentry must be able to read this release's stacks. Kenneth gives you
`SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT` and a read-only
`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`; set them in the shell only, never in a file. From the
release worktree, on the Mac for the disk image and the unpacked Windows
portable zip (its `JusPrin/` folder), and on the Linux VM for the AppImage
(`--appimage-extract` only works on Linux; that VM needs a checkout of the
release commit and node):

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh verify <file>` on
  the Mac app's `Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer`, Windows' `OrcaSlicer.dll` and
  the AppImage's `squashfs-root/bin/orca-slicer` must print "Sentry holds
  debug information".
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh verify <folder>` on
  the Mac app's `Contents/Resources`, the Windows zip's `JusPrin/resources`
  and `squashfs-root/resources` must say Sentry holds both pages' source
  maps.
- The app cannot cause an error report on purpose, and Help › Report a
  problem opens a GitHub issue, not a Sentry report. If an unexpected error
  happens while testing, send it and check in Sentry, under release
  `JusPrin <version> (OrcaSlicer <SoftFever_VERSION from version.inc>)`, that
  the app's frames show function, file and line. Otherwise say it was not
  done.

`winget_updater.yml`, inherited from OrcaSlicer, would submit the installer
to winget as `SoftFever.OrcaSlicer` on publish. `gh workflow list --all` must
show it `disabled_manually`; if not, tell Kenneth before he publishes.

Tell Kenneth what was tested on which platform. He publishes.

## 11. After publishing

- Start the previous release and check that Preferences › Updates offers the
  new one. The update check reads only published releases.
- With Kenneth's yes, reply to and close the issues the release fixes, and
  open a Homebrew cask pull request if JusPrin's cask is in Homebrew
  (`brew info --cask jusprin`).
- In Sentry, a new report's or crash's stack must name the app's functions
  with file and line, and a page error's frames the pages' sources
  (`AgentUI/src/...`, `HomeUI/src/...`). Bare addresses or
  `app:///home/index.html` positions mean a platform's debug files or a map
  are missing: run the verify scripts on that platform's released files.
- The next day, run the `jusprin-production-check` skill in tsd-enterprise.
- Remove your worktree and branch.

JusPrin 2.0.1 speaks your language, connects more printers from the printer chat, and fixes printers that could not be added in languages that write decimals with a comma.

## New

- **JusPrin in your language.** JusPrin's own screens, the AI chat and Home are translated into the 22 languages OrcaSlicer ships. Choose the language in Preferences › Appearance › Language. Numbers follow it too, for example "0,4 mm" in German. The translations are made by machine, so some wording may read oddly.
- **More printers connect from the printer chat.** The printer chat can now connect every connection type OrcaSlicer's printer settings offer, not only Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint. This includes Elegoo Centauri Carbon and Centauri Carbon 2 printers (Elegoo Link). The chat cannot finish Repetier, UltiMaker, or PrusaLink with a user name and password, and tells you where to set those up instead. Obico, SimplyPrint and 3DPrinterOS still need their own sign-in.
- **Reporting errors.** When something goes wrong that you can't fix yourself, JusPrin shows one message, "Something went wrong on our side". You can see the whole report, then press Report to JusPrin team, or tick "From now on, report errors like this automatically". You can also turn this on or off in Preferences › Updates › Error reports. It is off until you turn it on.

## Fixed

- In languages that write decimals with a comma, such as German, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Russian, the add-printer form showed no nozzle sizes for most printers, so the printer could not be added. Bed sizes such as 233.5 mm were also read as 233 mm, and a 0.4 mm nozzle in an opened 3MF file was read as 0. This always happened on Windows.
- A calibration test started from one of your projects lost that project and its chat.
- A project could save itself again after sitting idle, with nothing changed.
- A file the AI chat refused to attach (too large, or a kind it can't read) stopped the project from saving until you removed it.
- If JusPrin couldn't write its settings file, signing in or saving an API key looked like it worked, and was lost when you quit. JusPrin now shows an error instead.
- Deleting your account now waits until AI has finished replying in any chat.
- A chat whose account or API key was removed showed the wrong model in its greyed-out model picker. It now shows the model the chat ran on.
- When AI prepared a print, it could keep checking the slice it had just started, again and again, while the slice ran.

## What JusPrin now sends

- **When the app starts**, it tells JusPrin's server once that it started: a random number made on the first start, the app's version and the name of your operating system. Nothing in it names you, and no sign-in goes with it. It is not sent in stealth mode.
- **Error reports and crashes** go to JusPrin's error tracker (Sentry) only when you press Report to JusPrin team, or when you have turned on automatic reports. A report holds where in the app the error happened, the steps just before it (never what you typed or what AI said), your operating system and the app's log for that run. A crash report also holds the app's state at the moment it crashed. With automatic reports off, a crash report stays on your computer.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

277	* Don't Crash or Stay Silent When the OpenGL Context Can't Be Activated
278	
279	When the driver refuses to make the OpenGL context current, no ImGui frame ever runs and
280	OpenGL is never initialized, so ImGui has no current font and the GL functions are never
281	loaded. A notification that measures its text from an event handler (a validation warning, a
282	job's progress, the slicing progress bar) then reads the null font and crashes, and once a
283	slice completes, loading its G-code preview calls the unloaded GL functions and crashes too.
284	
285	Notifications now skip measuring until a frame has set up the font; they stay Unknown, and
286	render() already measures them when it draws. The G-code preview is not loaded while OpenGL
287	cannot be initialized; with OpenGL up, init_opengl() returns at once and nothing changes.
288	
289	On Windows, a shown canvas whose context cannot be made current is reported once: wx drops the
290	wglMakeCurrent error in release builds, so the call is repeated to log GetLastError() with the
291	canvas's pixel format and the display it is on. If OpenGL never came up in the session, the
292	user gets one error dialog instead of an empty 3D view with no explanation. A GTK canvas can
293	fail until its surface is mapped, so other platforms only get the crash fixes.
294	
295	* Name the Display Adapter Instead of Only Suggesting a Driver Upgrade When OpenGL Can't Be Activated
296	
297	A context that can't be made current has several causes: no OpenGL driver
298	behind the display the window is on (a disabled adapter, or one running on
299	the Microsoft Basic Display Adapter), a broken driver, or an overlay. The old
300	advice to upgrade the driver covered only one of them. The dialog now names
301	the adapter Windows reports for the window's display and lists the general
302	checks, and the log line keeps the display device and adapter name.

input.content:
JusPrin 2.0.2 can run its AI chats on a model on your own computer, lets AI add holes and parts to your models, and tells you clearly what to do when your own AI account refuses a request.

## New

- **AI on your own computer.** Chats can run on a model in Ollama or LM Studio, with no account and no credits. Set it up in Preferences › BYOAI › A model on this computer: press Find models, pick one, and press Use this model. JusPrin checks that the model can use the app's tools and has a context of at least 32k. It then shows under "On this computer" in each chat's model menu. Web search is not available for these chats, and a model that cannot see pictures is sent none.
- **AI can add holes and parts.** Ask AI for a screw hole, a slot, a peg or a lip, and it adds boxes or cylinders to your object, as solid parts or as holes. One Undo removes them. Asked for text or a logo, AI gives you the steps to add it yourself; a logo must be an SVG file.
- **AI can change your printer's hardware settings,** such as the bed size, the nozzle and the number of extruders. Before, it told you to change them by hand.
- **More printers connect from the printer chat.** For a Flashforge printer in LAN Only mode, PrusaLink with a user name and password, or Repetier, the chat opens a form that asks for the serial number, access code, login or printer name. What you type goes only to the printer; AI does not see it. Only UltiMaker still has to be set up in the printer settings window.
- **Home tells you when a new version is out.** A card at the top of Home's right column says which version is available. See what's new shows the release notes, Open download page opens the download page, and you can choose Remind me tomorrow or Skip this version.
- **OrcaSlicer's message boxes go into the chat.** In the JusPrin view, messages such as a failed printer connection or a refused print job now show in the project's chat instead of in a box over the app. Switching printer, filament or process while settings are changed no longer asks "Transfer or discard changes": JusPrin saves a version of the project first, so Version history keeps your changes, and the chat says which profiles the settings now follow.
- **Clearer messages when your own AI account refuses.** With your own key for OpenAI, OpenRouter or Anthropic, JusPrin now says when the account is out of credits, when the key is not allowed, or when the chat is too long for the model. When the service explains a refusal itself, JusPrin shows its words, for example "OpenRouter says: …". When the service is down or overloaded, JusPrin says it could not reach the service, instead of "Something went wrong on our side".
- **About 200 more sentences are translated,** including the titles of AI's actions in the chat, setting values in the Changes list, and the printer chat's first message.

## Fixed

- On Windows, quitting JusPrin crashed when error reports were turned on.
- On Windows in German and other languages, Ask AI about filament settings opened an empty chat with "Something went wrong on our side".
- On Windows in French, Spanish or Portuguese, a chat whose title had an accented letter, such as "Problème", failed to send.
- A chat whose reply stopped during a web search could not be continued: every next message failed.
- When AI switched to another printer with more filaments than that printer takes, the printer was switched and then the setup failed half done. It is now refused before anything changes.
- AI could end a chat with "cannot run (invalid_arguments)" after writing a note that was too long. It is now told which text was too long and the limit, and shortens it.
- Import printers from OrcaSlicer stayed on "Importing…" with every button greyed out after Cancel on the unsaved-changes question.
- On Linux with Wayland and an Intel graphics card, the Preview, Device and Project tabs could freeze.
- On Windows, when the 3D view could not start OpenGL, JusPrin could crash or show an empty 3D view. It now says which graphics card it found and what to check.
- In Preferences › BYOAI, when connecting an outside AI app such as Claude Code failed, the message gave no next step. It now says to copy the command and run it yourself, with a Copy button.
- Many messages written for AI were shown to you instead, such as "A hello handshake is required". Typing a message and then opening an earlier chat lost what you typed. Resume on an earlier chat failed after a slice. "Revert to here" opened a "Revert failed" window, and pressing the slice button twice opened "Couldn't slice".
- A photo in HEIC format renamed to .jpg is now refused when you attach it, instead of failing the chat.
- A project whose chats were saved by a newer JusPrin now says so in the chat, instead of showing no chats.

## What JusPrin now sends

- **Error reports and crashes** now carry your JusPrin account number when you are signed in, or else the random number this install made on its first start, so we can tell how many people a problem hits. Your email is not sent. Reports are still sent only when you press Report to JusPrin team, or when you have turned on automatic reports.
- **A chat on a model on your computer** is sent only to the address you entered in Preferences, not to JusPrin or any AI service.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

# JusPrin Linux GUI test VM

A GCP VM for building JusPrin on Linux and testing its GUI, either by hand over
remote desktop or by script on a headless display.

| | |
|---|---|
| Instance | `jusprin-linux-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-west2-a` (Los Angeles, for low latency from California) |
| Machine | n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB), 300 GB pd-balanced, no GPU |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, XFCE desktop |
| Toolchain | Ubuntu's gcc 13, CMake 4.3.0 (same as the CI runner, in /opt), Node 24.11.1 (in /opt) |
| Checkout | `~/JusPrin` on branch `jusprin-dev` (user `kenneth`) |
| OpenGL | Mesa llvmpipe, OpenGL 4.5 core, software rendering |

The VM has no service account, so it cannot call GCP APIs. It cannot fetch the
private GitHub repo either; send commits with a git bundle (below).

## Scripts (run on the Mac)

- `./vmssh.sh '<command>'` runs a command on the VM.
- `./vmscp.sh <src> <dst>` copies files; write `VM:~/path` for the VM side.
- `./connect-rdp.sh` starts the VM if stopped, prints the login, and holds an SSH
  tunnel open. Point Windows App (Microsoft Remote Desktop) at `localhost:33890`,
  user `kenneth`. xrdp listens only on the VM's own localhost, so the project-wide
  `default-allow-rdp` firewall rule does not expose it.
- `env.sh` holds the instance name and forces the `ai-agent` service account. It
  also points gcloud at uv's standalone Python 3.12, because Homebrew's Python lost
  its OpenSSL library when Homebrew moved from openssl@3 to openssl@4.

## Scripts (copied to the VM's home folder)

- `~/vm-run-app.sh [args]` starts the built app on headless display `:99` (Xvfb
  with the xfwm4 window manager) with data dir `~/jusprin-test-data`. Log:
  `~/app.log`. It sets `SSL_CERT_FILE`; without it OrcaSlicer's Linux build stops
  at startup on a dialog asking which certificate file to use.
- `~/vm-screenshot.sh` saves display `:99` to `~/shot.png`.
- Click with `DISPLAY=:99 xdotool mousemove X Y click 1`. Screenshot pixels equal
  screen coordinates (1920x1080).
- Stop the app with `pkill -x orca-slicer`. Never `pkill -f orca-slicer` over
  ssh: it matches the ssh command's own text and kills the session.

## Build

```bash
# First time on a fresh VM: deps (about 25 min) then app and tests (about 30 min)
cd ~/JusPrin && ./build_linux.sh -dst -j 16
# After code changes: app and tests only
cd ~/JusPrin && ./build_linux.sh -st -j 16
```

The app lands in `~/JusPrin/build/package/bin/orca-slicer`. Run long builds
detached so an ssh disconnect does not kill them:

```bash
setsid nohup bash -c 'set -o pipefail; ./build_linux.sh -st -j 16 2>&1 | tee ~/build.log; echo BUILD_EXIT=$? >> ~/build.log' >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null &
```

Tests: `cd ~/JusPrin/build && DISPLAY=:99 ctest -C Release -j 8`.

## Sending new commits

```bash
git bundle create f.bundle jusprin-dev ^<commit the VM already has>
./vmscp.sh f.bundle VM:~/
./vmssh.sh 'cd ~/JusPrin && git pull ~/f.bundle jusprin-dev'
```

## Cost

The VM bills while running. Stop it when idle:

```bash
gcloud compute instances stop jusprin-linux-test --project elegoo-backend --zone us-west2-a
```

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on each start; the scripts look it up
by name, so nothing needs editing.
# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

       gcloud compute instances stop   jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend
       gcloud compute instances update jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend --enable-display-device
       gcloud compute instances start  jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend

   Then 1920x1080 is available via set-res.ps1.

## Also required by this app

Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is NOT present on a clean Windows Server image.
Without it the app puts up a modal "WebView2 Runtime" prompt and startup blocks
forever. Installed here as 152.0.4191.66 via the Evergreen bootstrapper:

    Invoke-WebRequest "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703" -OutFile setup.exe
    .\setup.exe /silent /install

This matters more for JusPrin than for stock Orca, since JusPrin's UI is
WebView-based.

## Files

    startup.ps1      GCE windows-startup-script-ps1: OpenSSH, port 22 firewall,
                     authorized_keys, calls autologon.ps1. Runs every boot.
    autologon.ps1    Creates guitest + sets AutoAdminLogon. Idempotent.
    harness.ps1      Invoke-InSession / Take-Screenshot. Source this first.
    screenshot.ps1   Screen capture. Must run in-session.
    probe.ps1        Lists session 1's real windows to C:\guitest\windows.txt.
    focus-app.ps1    Closes leftover task consoles, maximizes the app window.
    click.ps1        Clicks the "x,y" in C:\guitest\click.txt.
    set-res.ps1      Sets 1920x1080. Must run in-session.
    install-app.ps1  Downloads the app, places the Mesa DLLs beside the .exe.
    run-app.cmd      Launches the app with llvmpipe forced, detached.
    winssh.sh        ssh wrapper. winscp.sh: scp wrapper.

## Typical cycle

    ./winscp.sh <local.ps1> guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Invoke-InSession -TaskName "X" ...'
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Take-Screenshot'
    ./winscp.sh guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/shot.png ./shot.png

## Known gap

There is no current JusPrin Windows binary to test. The Build all workflow's
Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with "could not find any
instance of Visual Studio"; last green Windows build was 2026-03-04 and its
artifacts have expired. Either fix that job, or install VS Build Tools on this VM
and build from the cached OrcaSlicer_dep_win64 artifact.
# Building JusPrin from source on the Windows VM

Verified 2026-09-07: full build from a clean VM, then run and screenshotted.
Total ~1h10m of machine time on n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB).

    deps build   22.7 min   (all 24 applicable deps from source)
    slicer build 23.0 min
    output       C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release\orca-slicer.exe (261 KB launcher)
                 + OrcaSlicer.dll (122.7 MB — the actual application)

## Order of operations

1. `install-buildtools.ps1` — CMake 4.3.5 (CI pins ~4.3.0), Ninja, Git for
   Windows, Strawberry Perl, and VS 2022 Build Tools with the VCTools workload.
2. Clone the repo (public, no credentials needed). Shallow is fine: the version
   comes from `version.inc`, not git tags.
3. `build-deps-full.ps1` — builds all deps. **Do not use the CI dependency
   artifact**; see below.
4. `build-slicer.ps1` — runs `build_release_vs.bat slicer`.
5. Put Mesa where the app looks for it, then `run-jusprin.cmd`.

## Things that will bite you

**Run long builds as a SCHEDULED TASK, not over SSH.** Windows OpenSSH kills the
whole process tree when the session ends, so a build started from an SSH command
(even detached with Start-Process) dies on disconnect. Register it instead:

    New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "SYSTEM" -LogonType ServiceAccount -RunLevel Highest

Two builds racing in one directory corrupt each other — OpenSSL failed with
`C1033: cannot open program database ossl_static.pdb` when that happened here.

**awk must be on PATH.** `deps/PNG/PNG.cmake` passes `-DPNG_PREFIX=prusaslicer_`,
so libpng generates `pngprefix.h` with an awk script. Without awk you get
`AWK-NOTFOUND` in the PNG CMakeCache and then `C1083: Cannot open include file:
'pngprefix.h'`. Git for Windows ships awk — add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin`
to PATH, not just `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd`.

**Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5`.** Several bundled CMakeLists still
declare pre-3.5 minimums, which CMake 4.x rejects outright.

**The CI dependency artifact is unusable.** `OrcaSlicer_dep_win64_20260906`
contains a bundle built 2025-10-17, before `deps/Eigen` was added. The source
requires Eigen 5.0.1 and CMake fails at configure with "Could not find a package
configuration file provided by Eigen3". Build deps from source instead.

**Never hard-stop the VM mid-build.** Stopping the instance during the deps build
left 622 of 22,011 installed files as NUL bytes. It surfaced as bogus syntax
errors deep in Boost headers. Detect it with:

    Get-ChildItem $prefix -Recurse -Include *.hpp,*.h,*.cmake |
      # read first 4 KB, flag any file containing byte 0

The fix is a clean rebuild; DL_CACHE keeps all 21 source archives, so it is a
recompile, not a re-download.

**Qhull is expected to be missing.** `deps/CMakeLists.txt` comments it out under
`if (MSVC)` ("Experimental"), so 24 built deps is the complete set on Windows.

## Running it — use the app's own Mesa hook

Do NOT drop opengl32.dll next to the exe. `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` already
handles this: when system OpenGL is below 2.0 it loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll`
itself and prints "MESA OpenGL library was loaded successfully".

    build\src\Release\mesa\opengl32.dll      <- Mesa's, the app loads this
    build\src\Release\libgallium_wgl.dll     <- dependency, resolves from exe dir

Still export `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`: the GCE
virtual display exposes a D3D12 device, and Mesa's d3d12 backend crashes on the
first rendered frame.

## Windows CI is broken for a different reason

`Build all`'s Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is NOT a bug in
`build_release_vs.bat` — the same script picks generator VS 17 2022 here from
`msbuild -version` (17.14.51.32402) and configures fine against a registered
Build Tools instance. The problem is the GitHub runner's environment.

JusPrin compiles from source on the Windows test VM and the built binary runs
with its Agent UI visible. Verified 2026-09-07 on n2-standard-16: deps 22.7 min,
slicer 23.0 min. Output is `orca-slicer.exe` (261 KB launcher) plus
`OrcaSlicer.dll` (122.7 MB). Full recipe in
`/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/vm-harness/windows/BUILDING.md`; VM setup in its README.
See [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]].

**Why:** four of the five failures below produce misleading errors far from
their cause, and two were self-inflicted by how the build was driven.

**How to apply:**
- Run long builds as a Windows **scheduled task** (SYSTEM / ServiceAccount), not
  over SSH — OpenSSH kills the process tree on disconnect. Never let two builds
  share a directory: that produced OpenSSL `C1033 cannot open program database`.
- Add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin` to PATH so **awk** is found, or libpng
  cannot generate `pngprefix.h` (`-DPNG_PREFIX=` in deps/PNG/PNG.cmake) and you
  get a confusing `C1083` on a header that was never written.
- Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` for CMake 4.x.
- **Do not use the CI deps artifact** — the shipped bundle predates `deps/Eigen`
  and cannot satisfy Eigen 5.0.1. Build deps from source.
- Never hard-stop the VM mid-build: doing so left 622 installed files full of
  NUL bytes and surfaced as fake syntax errors inside Boost headers.
- Qhull is deliberately excluded on MSVC (deps/CMakeLists.txt), so 24/25 is
  complete on Windows.
- To run headless, use the app's own hook rather than dropping DLLs beside the
  exe: `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` when
  system OpenGL < 2.0. Still force `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe`.

The `Build all` Windows CI job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is a GitHub runner
environment problem, not `build_release_vs.bat` — the same script selects the
same generator on the VM and configures fine against registered Build Tools.

**MSVC rejects `this` in a nested lambda's init-capture.** Found 2026-09-07 at
commit fbe5963b: `CallAfter([self=wxWeakRef<wxWindow>(this),...])` written INSIDE
another lambda compiled on clang but failed on MSVC with 37 errors, because MSVC
bound that `this` to the enclosing closure object, so it tried to build a
`wxWeakRef<wxWindow>` from a lambda pointer
(`Tracked_class_should_inherit_from_wxTrackable`). Name the object first —
`auto* menu = this;` then capture `menu`. Watch for this pattern whenever a
deferred callback is set up from within another lambda; it is invisible on macOS.

**PowerShell splits `-m:6` (2026-10-24).** In a .ps1, `& cmake --build … -- -m:6 -v:m`
reaches MSBuild as `-m:` `6` and fails at once ("For switch syntax, type
MSBuild -help"). Quote them: `'-m:6' '-v:m'`. Also `*>>` writes UTF-16, so
Select-String on that log matches nothing; use `2>&1 | Out-File -Encoding utf8`.
A watcher built from `winssh.sh 'powershell -Command "…\"…\"…"'` silently never
matched for 3 hours — the quoting rule above applies to status checks too.
Killing "my" processes by command-line match also took out a taskhostw.exe;
kill the PIDs your own task started (and their /T trees), not a pattern.

**Shell harness on the VM (2026-11-07, app-menus).** `C:\src\JusPrin\build\tests\shell\Release\shell_integration_harness.exe` has Mesa beside it; run it from a .cmd with `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` through an Interactive scheduled task as guitest; it uses its own temp data dir. Build it with `cmake --build build --config Release --target jusprin_web shell_integration_harness -- '-m:12'` (node is at `C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64`). The VM has no access to unpushed commits: send them with `git bundle create f.bundle <branch> ^<vm-head>`.
- MSVC also rejects a local `constexpr` used inside a lambda that doesn't capture it (C3493; clang accepts). Make it `static constexpr`.
- On jusprin-newui b0a2fe3b08 the default suite already fails 6 checks on Windows: three failed_autosave_* checks (the harness simulates a failed save by removing write permission, and Windows ignores that on folders), earlier_model_version_available, and agent_panel_columns_tile_the_client at 1000 and 1400 DIP. Compare against that list before blaming a change.
- In PowerShell, `[IO.File]` takes relative paths from the process folder, not from Set-Location; use absolute paths. In a .cmd, `echo exit=%ERRORLEVEL%>> f` turns `0>>` into a redirect; put a space before `>>`.

`us-west2-a`, n2-standard-16, 300 GB, Ubuntu 24.04 + XFCE. Harness and README at

render. Sibling of [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]]; container path is [[linux-arm-docker-build]].

**Why:** the traps below each cost a retry.

**How to apply:**
- `ai-agent` cannot attach the default compute service account; create VMs with
  `--no-service-account --no-scopes`.
- xrdp is bound to 127.0.0.1 and reached through an SSH tunnel (connect-rdp.sh,
  localhost:33890), because `default-allow-rdp` is open to 0.0.0.0/0 project-wide.
- The repo is private: send code as a git bundle. A bundle of `origin/jusprin-dev`
  stores `refs/remotes/origin/jusprin-dev`, so `git clone -b jusprin-dev` fails;
  fetch that ref explicitly.
- Set `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` or the app blocks at
  startup on a certificate-store dialog.
- After a start, xrdp can fail at boot (2026-11-11): systemd times out waiting
  for /run/xrdp/xrdp.pid, the folder is gone, and the tunnel prints "channel 2:
  open failed: connect failed: Connection refused". Fix:
  `sudo systemctl restart xrdp-sesman xrdp`, then `ss -ltn | grep 3389`.
- `pkill -f orca-slicer` over ssh kills the ssh session itself; use `pkill -x`.
- Homebrew moved openssl@3 to @4 on 2026-11-09 and broke gcloud's Python;
  env.sh sets CLOUDSDK_PYTHON to uv's standalone CPython 3.12.
- Landed 2026-11-09 as fdb873ad65 on jusprin-dev: the Linux test-configure fix
  (name the target in six `orcaslicer_copy_test_dlls()` calls), the CLI crash on a
  filament without filament_diameter, and the Orca account file-time fix. Full
  Linux ctest then passes. VM checkout is on jusprin-dev at that commit.
- Linking tests/jusprin can race: shell_theme_tests and jusprin_fake_bambu_tests
  both copy the Python runtime into Release/python ("Error removing directory").
  Timing-dependent; rerunning the build passed.
- Wait loops on the VM must match a fresh log: an old ~/ctest.log with
  CTEST_EXIT made a wait finish at once with stale results.
- **The VM cannot show WebKit/Wayland rendering bugs (2026-11-19).** It runs X11
  (Xvfb/xrdp) with llvmpipe, and `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp` sets
  `WEBKIT_DMABUF_RENDERER_FORCE_SHM=1` whenever `is_hypervisor_guest()` is true,
  which is exactly the workaround for upstream issue 17381 (fixed by upstream PR
  17399, bf1fb93b78, not in JusPrin 2.0.1). A clean classic view on the VM is no
  evidence against a user's "garbled/unusable on Linux" report.

I checked the on-screen labels it quotes against the source. It needs your yes on the wording before it goes into the release commit, so you can read it now.

- **Server:** all 19 addresses the app calls answer on `jusprinv2.obico.io`, and a made-up address gets 404, so the server is not in maintenance mode. Two server behaviors this release relies on:
  - The sign-in check returns `user.id`, which it has done since July 2025.
  - The gateway's `request_too_large` answer for a chat that is too long for the model. It is on tsd-enterprise `master` as `ea0b788fac`, but I have not checked that it is deployed. If it isn't, those chats show "Something went wrong on our side", as they did in 2.0.1.

**Still running**

- An error-handling audit of the 33 app commits, and a second one of the six server commits since 2.0.1. The server one is needed because the release relies on that gateway change.

**Coming later, each needing your yes**
- The wording of the release notes.
- Which audit findings must be fixed before the release.
- A small paid prompt run on the app's default model; I'll give you its cost.
- The guide check. It drives the app on this Mac's screen, so nobody can use the computer while it runs.

A sub-reviewer checked the first two Ollama cases against the real Ollama 0.40.18 on this Mac; nothing was tried against LM Studio. I re-checked findings 3, 4 and 5 against the code myself. Four sub-reviewers covered the rest.

**Introduced by this range: should fix**

1. **A local model's own error is reported as ours.** `ProviderAgent.cpp:848` and `:856-859` (fd7127e424 with e8aee03faf). Someone picks a model too big for their memory, and Ollama answers 500 ("llama runner process has terminated"). Or they delete a model mid-chat, and Ollama answers 404 ("model 'x' not found"). Both end in "Something went wrong on our side" and a report. The failure is the person's: Ollama's words should be shown and nothing reported. The test at `test_local_model_setup.cpp:300` asserts today's behaviour.

2. **A wrong port, or an older Ollama, is reported as ours.** `LocalModelSetup.cpp:134-135` and `ProviderAgent.cpp:856` (fd7127e424). Port 5000 on a Mac answers 403 with an empty body, and any answer that isn't JSON goes the same way, to us. This is the person's mistake, and "Nothing is answering at…" fits.

3. **An outage at the person's own AI service is called a network problem.** `ProviderAgent.cpp:848-851` and `:919-923` (e8aee03faf). When the service answers 500 or above, or says it is overloaded, the person sees "The AI request could not reach the OpenAI service." That sentence also covers having no network, so they check their connection. The trouble is at the service, and the rules say to tell them that truthfully. The service's own words are dropped, and the commit quotes no yes from Kenneth for using the sentence this way.

4. **A save failure mid-work opens our report dialog.** `ShellController.cpp:1816-1823` (ed25d6d94a). This report call is not in a top handler. Someone with the cut tool open switches printer, the save fails with "Finish the current tool edit…", and they get "Something went wrong on our side". That failure is theirs. During an AI tool call the dialog opens, though the rules allow only a report with no dialog there. When opening a file, two windows show for one failure.

5. **A setup command's timeout is detected by English words.** `AgentHost.cpp:4518` searches for "timed out", and 3c27e9b3a0 translated that message in `McpSetupCommand.cpp:77,148`. In German, a timeout now reads "Copy the command and run it yourself." The warning that the client's config may already have changed is lost.

6. **A chat too long gets no next step.** `ProviderAgent.cpp:771-773, 787` (e109da5c29). The person sees "The request was too large for the OpenAI service." and is not told to start a new chat.

7. **Slice failures that are ours are never reported.** `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1025-1027` (ed25d6d94a). Every slice failure, including "Unknown C++ exception", becomes only a print issue. The missing report is older; the one branch for all owners is new. Disk-full export errors and custom G-code errors are the person's, so a "critical" flag alone can't split them.

8. **A late printer refusal can be dropped.** `ConnectionEvents.cpp:40` (ed25d6d94a). The "chat is waiting" mark is never cleared after the chat's 30-second timeout or a cancel. A later "Incorrect password" from the Bambu plug-in is then treated as already shown, and only logged.

9. **A failed kept-G-code export can name the wrong folder.** `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1338-1351` (e8aee03faf). `copy_file` names the target folder in its error on every platform, so every failure is shown as the person's, never ours. A failure reading our own copy shows the chosen folder's path. This is rare.

10. **Home's sign-in failures leave no log line.** `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:706-708`, missed by dbd73c7802. The server's answer (`error.said`) is dropped.

11. **The report for unreadable shipped profiles is thin.** `SetupOptionsLoader.cpp:78-80` (e8aee03faf). It names only the vendor and drops the failed files and the loader's error text.

**Introduced by this range: minor**

- `MessageRoutes.cpp:42` (ed25d6d94a) files every message OrcaSlicer shows as a failed chat entry, including "…switched successfully."
- `ToolRegistry.cpp:1916-1921` (a142e0b4f3): the new message counts characters, but the checks that refuse count UTF-8 bytes. A 90-character Chinese title is refused with no limit named.
- `ProviderProfile.hpp:103`: errors read "the model on this computer says…", though Ollama said it, not the model. The line also starts lowercase.
- `AgentHost.cpp:4185`: the sentence for a chat whose local model is gone has no test.
- `PreferencesWindow.cpp:283` (f52f37375d): a refused change stays on screen until the next state update.
- `LocalModelSetup.cpp:226`: "pick another model" often means "raise the context setting" (Kenneth approved that wording).
- `CloudSignInMachine.cpp:191` (e8aee03faf): "no answer" at sign-out may be our server timing out (inferred).

What checks out: the top handlers in `AgentHost::pump_setup` and `pump_stream` report and tell the person correctly. `report_unexpected_error` is otherwise called only from top handlers. The out-of-credits and "Name, then its words" sentences have tests and Kenneth's quoted yes.

**Older than this range, worth knowing**

- `CloudAccount.cpp:314`: no network and an unlisted refusal from our server share "JusPrin couldn't sign you in".
- `CloudHttpResult` drops response headers, so no request id from our server reaches a report.
- `ServerSheet.cpp:86-96`: our server failing to give the billing link is never reported.</result>

<result>I found nothing in these server commits that blocks the 2.0.2 app build. There are six things that should be fixed and four minor ones. Commits 4156bf3d49 (log every failed request), dd34ba2b2c (only the JusPrin 2 app's token is accepted) and c257bbca05 (Latin-1 chat titles) came out clean. All seven commits are on `origin/release`. I did not check whether production is running them.

**Should fix**

1. **The Standard model's too-long chat still shows "Something went wrong on our side"** (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/gateway.py:496-512`, ea0b788fac). Standard chats go through OpenRouter to DeepSeek. OpenRouter's documentation says a 400 for a too-long chat carries the error code `invalid_prompt`, with no `response` wrapper. If it has an `error_type` at all, it sits at the top of the body, and the matcher never reads it there. So `names_chat_too_long` misses it, and the chat lands in the "anything else" branch: the person sees our generic sentence, and we get a Sentry report. The failure is the person's, and the rule says they should get `request_too_large`. Expert chats (Anthropic's "prompt is too long") and OpenRouter's mid-reply `response.failed` are matched correctly. I checked this by reading the code against OpenRouter's documentation. Sentry has no such report in the last 14 days. The fix is server-only, so the app can ship without waiting for it.
2. **Reports of a refused app request don't say which check refused it** (`errors.py:84` `super().__init__(code)`, raised again at `gateway.py:198-201`, 29445fd705). The failure is ours, and it now reaches us. But I ran `GatewayError` and its text is only the code, so both the Sentry title and the log line read `GatewayError: invalid_request`. The specific reason, such as "The X-JusPrin-Chat header must be 32 lowercase hex digits.", is lost. The rule says the report must keep the error text.
3. **Payment success page when the browser is signed out** (`web.py:412`, 29445fd705). The person sees "This link has expired. Go back to JusPrin and open the page again." with status 410, and is not told whether the payment went through. Someone buying a credit pack might pay twice. The code treats this as the person's, but it could also be the app's web view losing its cookie, which would be ours. Unverified.
4. **A real code whose coupon set is missing from `JUSPRIN_V2_LOYALTY_OFFERS`** (`ledger/billing.py:97-98`, 65dd4972f0). The person is told the code isn't recognized, exactly as for a mistyped code. That case is our configuration, so it should come to us. Nothing is logged. Checked by reading.
5. **Subscriber checkout refused** (`web.py:397`, 65dd4972f0). If the code was used in the meantime, or the account already has a plan, the person lands back on an empty code box with nothing said. Nothing is logged, so neither they nor we learn anything.
6. **Print-report refusals, now 500** (`views.py:266`, 29445fd705). These are now reported, but Sentry drops request bodies over 10 KB, and a report with photos always is. So when the report's facts JSON can't be read, Sentry won't show the text that failed. Unverified.

**Minor**

- None of 65dd4972f0's new outcomes are written to the log: unknown code, used-up code, account already on a plan, signed out on the code page.
- The new code-page sentences have tests in `test_loyalty.py`. But the commit quotes Kenneth's yes for the approach and the wording rule, not for each sentence, and nothing counts how often each is shown.
- `web.py:438` says "first month free" after any checkout whose first invoice was $0, not only one bought with a code. Unverified whether that can happen.

input.recap: Tests pass on Mac, Linux, both pages and both prompt suites, and both audits found nothing that blocks the release. Windows tests are still running. A fix that lets the shell harness build on Linux is committed locally only, and nothing is pushed.
input.ask: Which error-handling findings should be fixed before 2.0.2?

content.text:
The 2.0.2 release is tested and audited on everything except Windows, and nothing found so far blocks it. Windows tests are still running on the VM. Five decisions below are yours before I can go on.

**Results**
- **Mac:** all 3969 tests pass. The page tests pass too: 845 for the Agent page, 169 for Home.
- **Linux:** all 3978 tests pass, including the 7 that need the built app.
- **Prompt suites on the Claude subscription:** the project chat passed 66 of 66 runs, with no case worse than its baseline. The printer chat passed 78 of 78.
- **Server:** every address the app calls answers.
- **Shell harness on Linux:** `snapshot_web_view` takes optional pictures and exists only on Mac and Windows, but `f52f37375d` calls it from code Linux also compiles. So the harness test program no longer compiled on Linux, and `build_linux.sh -st` failed. I fixed it as commit `1cce275de0`, on its own branch from `origin/jusprin-dev`, and confirmed on the Linux VM that the harness now builds. It is not pushed.

**Decision needed: which error-handling findings to fix before the release?** The app audit found 11 places where a failure goes to the wrong person. None blocks the release. Four of them come from features new in this release, and one is a translation bug:
- an error from Ollama itself, such as a model too big for memory, is reported as ours;
- a wrong port is reported as ours, instead of "Nothing is answering at…";
- a failed save while switching printer opens our report dialog, though the failure is the person's;
- the setup command's timeout is found by looking for the English words "timed out", so in German a timeout shows the wrong line;
- a chat too long for the model gets no "start a new chat".

Fixing these five takes a few hours, and every check before the release runs again afterwards. The other six are older or rare, and can go into 2.0.3. My pick is to fix the five now.

**Decision needed: what should the app say when the person's own AI service is down?** Today an outage at OpenAI, OpenRouter or Anthropic reads "The AI request could not reach the … service." That is also what people see with no network, so they check their own connection. My pick is a new sentence: "The OpenAI service is having trouble right now. Try again later." Do you approve that sentence, or would you rather keep today's for 2.0.2?

**Decision needed: should the release take in `abc6c9e500` and the harness fix?** `abc6c9e500` landed on `jusprin-dev` after I fixed the commit range, and changes only the release skill's text. Taking both in means pushing `1cce275de0` to `jusprin-dev` and rebasing the release branch onto it. That costs nothing extra, because the checks rerun anyway if the five fixes go in. My pick is yes, and to push.

**Decision needed: may I spend about $1–3 on the paid prompt run?** The suite's guide asks for a small paid run, before a release, on the app's default model, `gpt-5.4-mini`. My estimate is about $1–3: both suites, two runs per case, at $0.75 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output, plus the judge.

**Decision needed: is the release notes wording right?** The draft is [2.0.2.md](.claude/worktrees/release-2.0.2/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/2.0.2.md). It leaves out one fix, `ed789c5613`: the Mac app's bundled Python no longer needs Homebrew's compression library. I doubt anyone notices, so my pick is to keep it out. Should it go in?

**Also open**
- The server audit found that a too-long Standard chat, which goes through OpenRouter to DeepSeek, still reaches us as an unexpected error. It also found that the server's reports of refused requests lose the reason. Both are server-only fixes, so the app can ship without them.
- I haven't checked whether production runs the server's `request_too_large` change.

Which audit findings should be fixed before 2.0.2: the five I picked, or all eleven?

Sources: [GPT-5.4 mini pricing (OpenAI)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.4-mini)

input.title: Fix 2.0.2 error-handling findings, after Kenneth confirms

input.prompt:
Fix six error-handling problems in JusPrin (repository /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin, a fork of OrcaSlicer), found by an audit of the commits going into the 2.0.2 release. The rules are the "Error handling" section of `AGENTS.md`.

FIRST, before changing any code: list each problem for Kenneth in plain words. Say what a person does, what they see today, whose failure it is under the rules, and the fix you propose, including any new sentence a person would see. Then wait for his confirmation. Fix only what he confirms, with his words quoted in the commit message wherever a new sentence needs his yes (AGENTS.md requires that).

The six problems, as the audit reported them (verify each against the code yourself; line numbers are at commit b946c73f5b):

1. An error from a local model's own app is reported as ours. `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp` around :848 and :856-859, from commit fd7127e424 together with e8aee03faf. A model too big for memory makes Ollama answer 500 ("llama runner process has terminated"). A model deleted mid-chat makes it answer 404 ("model 'x' not found"). Both show "Something went wrong on our side" and send a report. Under the rules the failure is the person's: show Ollama's own words, and do not report. The test at `tests/.../test_local_model_setup.cpp:300` asserts today's behaviour. A helper agent checked this against a real Ollama 0.40.18 on this Mac; LM Studio was not tried.
2. A wrong port, or an older Ollama, is reported as ours. `LocalModelSetup.cpp:134-135` and `ProviderAgent.cpp:856`. Port 5000 on a Mac answers 403 with an empty body, and any non-JSON answer goes the same way. The approved sentence "Nothing is answering at <address>. 13:## Before a release
14-
15-The guide is brought in line with the app before each release, on a computer with the app built.
16-
17-1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit to release: the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets.
18-2. Leave the computer alone and run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. It takes about a minute a page, plus the questions.
19-3. Fix what it reports, then run it again until it passes:
20-   - **A label is on no screen.** The app's wording changed. Find the new wording in the app and correct the page.
21-   - **A run failed.** Open its log, which the command names. Either the screen no longer works as the page says, and the page needs correcting, or the harness expects something the app no longer does, and the harness needs correcting.
22-   - **A picture is blank.** The program that started the command may not record the screen. Grant it Screen Recording in the system's privacy settings and run again.
23-   - **AI answered a question wrongly.** Read its reply in the output. Usually the page is unclear or its first line does not say when to read it.
24-4. Look through what changed on screen since the last release (`git log <last release tag>..HEAD -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`). The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new screen or menu item that no page mentions, so add those by hand.
25-5. Commit the pages together with their pictures, the skills the command rebuilt, and `checked-version.txt`. When every step passes for every page, the command writes the app's version to that file. A run with `--skip-app`, with `--area`, or without `--ask-ai` leaves it as it was. The release workflow refuses a version this file does not name. The file says the check passed for that version, not on which commit, so run it on the commit you mean to release.
26-
27-## What the command does
28-
29-1. **Walks the app and takes the pictures.** `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` names, for each page, the runs of the app's test harness that go through the screens the page describes, and the checks in each run the page depends on. `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py` runs them in the app as built and copies the pictures a page uses into `pictures/<page>/`.
30-2. **Rebuilds the copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from each page.
31-3. **Checks each page**, in `guide.test.ts` beside it: every label in bold is in the app's source, every section has a run in step 1, every picture is one step 1 took, and the page has questions for step 4. `components/Guide.test.tsx` checks that the app's guide window lists every page and shows each with all its pictures and without the parts written for AI.
32-4. **Asks AI the page's questions** (`--ask-ai`). `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` holds them with what a right answer says. `tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py` asks the model and has a judge read the replies.
33-
34-## Writing a page
35-
36-- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it. The model reads every page's description together in one list, and the Claude command-line tool that `--ask-ai` runs through cuts a tool description longer than about 2,000 characters, so keep each one short: about 200 bytes. Write `...` rather than `…` in it, since that tool rewrites the one as the other.
37-- Put words that are only for AI in `<!-- ai: … -->`. They are hidden on this site.
38-- Use bold only for words that are on screen, exactly as they are on screen.
39-- A picture goes on a line of its own, as `![what it shows](pictures/<page>/<name>.png)`, and comes from a run named in `guide_checks.json`. AI's copy leaves it out.
40-- A picture is kept at twice the screen's size, and the guide window shows it at half, the size it has on screen. Mark a run's picture that the harness draws at the screen's own size with `"atScreenSize": true`, and the command doubles it.
41-- List a new page at the top of this file, or the guide window leaves it out.
42-- Give each `##` section a run in `guide_checks.json`.
43-- Add at least three questions for the page to `guide_questions.json`.
44-- AI's copy may hold at most 16 KiB. Split a page that grows past that.
2.0.1

When a project file brought its own printer, the printer is marked **From the file · not one of your printers**.

## Choose the filament and its colour

Click the filament in the header. The menu has:

- **COLOUR**: click a colour to set the filament's colour. The + after them (**Other colour…**) opens a colour picker.
- **FILAMENTS FOR THIS PRINTER**: click one to print with it, or **Other filament…** to pick from all of them.
- **Use what's loaded on the printer…**, when the printer reports what is loaded in it.
- **Filament settings…**, **Ask AI about filament settings…** and **Calibrate this filament…**.

To print in two or more filaments, click **Add another filament to this print**. The menu then lists each filament by its number; click one to choose its filament and colour. To say which filament an object prints in, use **Change filament** in its menu in the Plates tab.

![The filament menu, with the colours, the filaments for this printer, and Add another filament to this print](pictures/printers-and-filament/filament-menu.png)

## The Printer menu

The **Printer** menu has the same commands for the open project: **Add a printer…**, **Printer settings…**, **Ask AI about printer settings…**, **Filament settings…**, **Ask AI about filament settings…** and **Calibrate…**. It works from Home too.

With no printer chosen yet, **Printer settings…** starts adding a printer instead, and **Calibrate…** is greyed out.

## Add a printer

1. On Home, click **+ Add printer** at the top of the printers, or choose **Add a printer…** in the **Printer** menu. A chat titled **Add a printer** opens.
2. Say which printer you have, in your own words, or pick it from a list: **Browse the full printer list** at the top of the chat opens a form that asks **Which printer?** and then **Which plate is on it?**.
3. The printer is saved under its own name and shows on Home. You can add two printers of the same model; each gets a name of its own.

If you skipped choosing a printer the first time JusPrin started, it uses a stand-in, a generic 250 mm Klipper printer, until you add yours.

## Connect a printer

Connecting a printer lets JusPrin send prints to it and show how it is doing. JusPrin connects Bambu Lab printers, and printers it reaches at an address on your network, such as Klipper printers through Moonraker, OctoPrint, PrusaLink and Elegoo Link.

1. On Home, click **Connect…** on the printer's card, or open the card's menu (**Printer actions**) and choose **Connect…**.
2. The printer's chat asks for what it needs, such as its address. A Bambu Lab printer also needs its **Access code**, and a print host may need its **API key**. These stay on this computer.
3. **Help me find the code** explains where to find it on the printer.

A Bambu Lab printer needs Bambu's network plug-in. The chat says so when it is missing.

## Rename or remove a printer

Open the printer card's menu on Home (**Printer actions**):

- **Rename**, then type the new name under **Printer name** and click **Save**. A name cannot be empty, hold any of < > [ ] : / \ | ? * ", or be the name of another printer.
## Connect an AI tool you already use

An AI app such as Claude Code or Codex can work on the project open in JusPrin.

1. In Preferences, open **BYOAI**. Under **Connect an AI tool you already use**, each tool says whether it was found on this computer. **Look again** searches again.
2. Click **Connect…** beside the tool. For some tools JusPrin shows a command to run, with **Copy**; for others it shows the change it will make to the tool's settings, and **Connect** makes it.
3. When it says **Connected**, click **Done**. The tool can now see and change the open project.

name: orca-inherited-teardown-crash
description: "Exiting OrcaSlicer/JusPrin with model volumes loaded segfaults in ~GLCanvas3D → Selection::clear → destroyed Plater::priv; inherited, not a fork regression"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-08-30T01:57:24.158Z
---

On the jusprin-newui branch, quitting the app while model volumes are loaded
can crash: `~GLCanvas3D → reset_volumes → Selection::clear →
Plater::canvas3D()` dereferences the already-destroyed `Plater::priv`
(`this=0x0` at Plater.cpp `get_current_canvas3D`). Crash reports with the
identical signature exist from 2026-08-28, before the Phase 1 shell change,
so treat it as inherited upstream teardown fragility, not a regression. GUI
test harnesses (tests/workspace, tests/shell) end their scenarios on an empty

"""One harness run. Returns whether the page's part of it passed, what
    failed in that part, how many checks passed, and what failed elsewhere.

    An entry with "checks" depends on those named checks alone: the run is
    stopped once they have passed, and a failure elsewhere in it is reported
    apart, since it is not about the page. Without "checks" the whole run
    has to pass. The harness gives up by itself after 900 s."""
    args = [str(out) if arg == "{dir}" else arg for arg in entry["args"]]
    env = dict(os.environ, **{name: str(out) if value == "{dir}" else value for name, value in entry.get("env", {}).items()})
    needed = set(entry.get("checks", []))
    if needed:
        # A run stopped early never removes its data folder, which the harness makes in the
        # temporary folder: put that beside the run, to remove it here. Only for these runs:
        # the printer menu's run takes ten minutes instead of six seconds with it moved.
        env["TMPDIR"] = str(out / "data")
        (out / "data").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    passed, failed, lines = set(), [], []
    process = subprocess.Popen([str(binary), *args], env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                               text=True, errors="replace")
    for line in process.stdout:
        lines.append(line)
        check = re.search(r"HARNESS CHECK (\S+) (PASS|FAIL)", line)
        if check:
            (passed.add if check.group(2) == "PASS" else failed.append)(check.group(1))
        if needed and (needed <= passed or needed & set(failed)):
            process.terminate()
            break
    process.wait()
    text = "".join(lines)
    log.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    shutil.rmtree(out / "data", ignore_errors=True)
    if needed:
        missing = sorted(needed - passed)
        return not missing, [f"{name} did not pass" for name in missing], len(passed), [name for name in failed if name not in needed]
    return "HARNESS RESULT PASS" in text, failed + re.findall(r"HARNESS ERROR (.+)", text), len(passed), []

content.text:
**What stopped me:** two limits. My own usage limit ran out in the middle of that turn, so I stopped and listed what was left. Separately, the Claude subscription that the guide check uses for its AI questions hit its session limit, which reset at 8:40 pm. Both have reset, and I've picked the work back up.

**The two local-model fixes are already pushed.** The fix session put them in one commit, `0f15457d27`, and `origin/jusprin-dev` already ends at it, so there was nothing left to push.

**The two failed guide runs are fixed.** Both failures were in the test harness, which had fallen behind two changes in this release. Neither was in the app.
- **Sign in to a JusPrin account:** the harness's stand-in server answered the sign-in check without an account number. Since `bc68055371`, the app treats that as our bug and stops. The real server has always sent the number, so I added one to the stand-in.
- **Settings for one plate:** the run switched the main window to OrcaSlicer's Preview page. Since `ed25d6d94a`, the JusPrin view refuses that switch. Check print isn't affected: it's a window of its own with its own preview. The run now checks that the switch is refused and that the left pane stays.

Both runs failed on the release build before the fix and pass after it. The fix is commit `07b6eceade` on branch `claude/harness-guide-runs`, made from `origin/jusprin-dev`. It is not pushed.

**One thing still open:** the "Sign in" run aborts as it exits, after every check passes. The guide check stops that run once its checks pass, so this doesn't affect it. macOS wrote no crash report for the abort, and I haven't found the cause or checked whether it also happens at 2.0.1.

**Decision needed: may I push `07b6eceade` and put 2.0.2 on top of today's `jusprin-dev`, which includes the local-model fixes?** You chose to release without those fixes. But they are now on `jusprin-dev`, and a release commit can land there only on top of them. So the choice is between two paths:
- **Include them:** I push `07b6eceade` and move the release branch onto it. Then I rerun everything the local-model commit could affect: the Mac tests, the Windows tests, the Linux tests and the guide check. That's roughly two to three hours of machine time. The release notes would also need a line for the fixes, which I'd show you.
- **Hold the release:** the release waits until you decide otherwise.

My pick is to include them, since the release can't reach `jusprin-dev` without them.
